headline: The Hotels & Lodging Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can explain a lodging's rules and equipment to others, handle hidden problems and improper requests, mediate between people in the right register, report incidents and emergencies clearly, and put a stay in writing in Spanish.

lessons.title: Explain the Hostel Kitchen and Locker System
lessons.objective: Explain in order how the shared kitchen labels, lockers and quiet hours work, and why each rule exists.

words.note: Peru and Mexico; Spain says el rotulador.
Peru; Mexico says el refrigerador.
Hostels also say el locker.
Feminine noun that takes el: el área común, las áreas comunes.
A woman is la voluntaria.

words.en: First, write your name and the date on the label.
words.es: Primero, escribe tu nombre y la fecha en la etiqueta.
words.note: Informal tú, guest to guest.

words.en: Then put your food on the shelf with your bed number.
words.es: Luego guarda tu comida en el estante con tu número de cama.

words.en: Lock your locker with a padlock, because the dorm is shared.
words.es: Cierra tu casillero con candado, porque el dormitorio es compartido.

words.en: That's why the kitchen closes at 10 at night.
words.es: Por eso la cocina cierra a las 10 de la noche.

words.en: Joaquín explained it all to me before his shift ended.
words.es: Joaquín me lo explicó todo antes de terminar su turno.

words.en: Now you explain it to me, to see if it's clear.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, para ver si quedó claro.
words.note: Informal; a friendly way to ask for a teach-back.

words.en: Excuse me, is the fridge cleaned every Sunday?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿la refrigeradora se limpia todos los domingos?
words.note: Formal, to the receptionist.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest who learned the hostel rules, and the AI is Valentina, a guest who just arrived: explain the kitchen labels, lockers and quiet hours in order with primero, luego, porque and por eso, then have her teach them back to you.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso)

examples.es: Primero pones la etiqueta y luego guardas la comida en la refrigeradora.
examples.en: First you put the label on, and then you put the food in the fridge.

examples.es: Los objetos de valor van en el casillero porque entra mucha gente al dormitorio.
examples.en: Valuables go in the locker because a lot of people come into the dorm.

lessons.title: Read the Casa Rural Manual for the Wood Stove
lessons.objective: Read the house manual for the wood stove and ventilation and confirm by phone that you understood it correctly.

words.note: How the stove draws air; regular el tiro = adjust the draft.
The fire-starter cubes sold in Spanish supermarkets.
A female owner; a man is el propietario. Spain also says la dueña.

words.en: I'll read step 3 aloud to you to confirm it.
words.es: Le leo el paso 3 en voz alta para confirmarlo.
words.note: Formal usted, to the owner.

words.en: It says here you open the vent before lighting it, is that right?
words.es: Aquí pone que se abre la rejilla antes de encender, ¿es así?
words.note: Spain: aquí pone = it says here.

words.en: Which vent, the one in the wall or the one on the stove?
words.es: ¿Qué rejilla, la de la pared o la de la estufa?

words.en: If it's lit at night, does the vent stay open?
words.es: Si se enciende de noche, ¿la rejilla se queda abierta?

words.en: If smoke comes into the room, what should you do?
words.es: Si sale humo a la habitación, ¿qué se hace?

words.en: I won't light it until it's clear to me.
words.es: No la enciendo hasta tenerlo claro.

words.en: According to your manual, first you open the vent and then you light it.
words.es: Según su manual, primero se abre la rejilla y luego se enciende.

words.en: Where is the dry firewood kept?

lessons.speaking: You are the guest in the cottage, and the AI is Covadonga, the owner, on the phone: read her wood stove instructions aloud, confirm each step with impersonal se and si + present (si se enciende…, se abre…), and ask before lighting anything.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (si se enciende la estufa, se abre la rejilla)

examples.es: Si se enciende la estufa, se abre la rejilla de ventilación.
examples.en: When the stove is lit, the air vent is opened.

examples.es: Las cenizas se vacían solo cuando están frías, según el manual.
examples.en: The ashes are emptied only when they're cold, according to the manual.

lessons.title: Teach a Friend the Building's Door and Key Fob Rules
lessons.objective: Teach a friend how to use the fob, the security door and the trash room, using commands, and check they got it.

words.note: Argentina: the building's front door onto the street.
Argentina: the building's doorman/super, often living on site.
Argentina; Mexico says el interfón.
Argentina: the hallway area by the elevator on each floor.
Argentina; Mexico says la bolsa de basura.
Argentina and Uruguay; Mexico says el bote.

words.en: Hold it against the reader and wait for the beep.
words.es: Apóyalo en el lector y espera el pitido.
words.note: In Buenos Aires you'll hear apoyalo (vos); the tú form is understood.

words.en: Close it properly when you come in; never leave it open.
words.es: Ciérrala bien al entrar; no la dejes abierta nunca.

words.en: Keep it safe, and if you lose it, tell the super.
words.es: Guárdalo bien, y si lo pierdes, avísale al encargado.

words.en: Don't open the street door for anyone you don't know.
words.es: No le abras la puerta de calle a nadie que no conozcas.

words.en: Take it down to the trash room; don't leave it on the landing.
words.es: Bájala al cuarto de la basura; no la dejes en el palier.

words.en: Okay, Martina, now you explain it to me.
words.es: A ver, Martina, explícamelo tú ahora.
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: Héctor, please correct me if I'm wrong.
words.es: Héctor, corríjame si me equivoco, por favor.
words.note: Formal usted, to the doorman.

words.en: Excuse me, Héctor, what time can the trash be taken down?
words.es: Perdón, Héctor, ¿a qué hora se puede bajar la basura?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are teaching the AI, your friend Martina, the building's entry rules: explain the fob, the security door and the trash room with commands like ciérrala, guárdalo and no la dejes abierta, then have her repeat the steps back to you.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (ciérrala, guárdalo, no la dejes abierta)

examples.es: Cuando entres, ciérrala detrás de ti.
examples.en: When you come in, close it behind you.

examples.es: Separa los reciclables y no los mezcles con la basura.
examples.en: Separate the recyclables and don't mix them with the trash.

lessons.title: Read the Spa Circuit Rules and Brief Your Friend
lessons.objective: Read the spa circuit rules and explain to a friend what to do before, during and after each pool and sauna.

words.note: Colombians often say las chancletas.
Spain; Latin America says la bata.
The word Spanish spa signs use for who should not use a facility.
Spain; Latin America says la presión arterial.
Always read it from the posted sign or ask staff.

words.en: Before going into the circuit, you have to put on the cap.
words.es: Antes de entrar en el circuito, hay que ponerse el gorro.

words.en: According to the sign, after the sauna you have to shower.
words.es: Según el cartel, después de la sauna hay que ducharse.

words.en: Felipe, before you go in, read the health warnings on the sign.
words.es: Felipe, antes de entrar, lee las contraindicaciones del cartel.
words.note: Informal tú, to a friend.

words.en: Since you take heart medication, ask the staff first.
words.es: Como tomas medicación para el corazón, pregúntale al personal primero.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Excuse me, what is the maximum time in the sauna?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿cuál es el tiempo máximo en la sauna?
words.note: Formal usted, to the attendant.

words.en: Excuse me, is this warning for people who take heart medication?
words.es: Perdone, ¿esta advertencia es para quien toma medicación cardíaca?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: It says here that after each bath you have to rest.
words.es: Aquí pone que después de cada baño hay que descansar.

words.en: If you feel dizzy, get out right away and tell Nuria.
words.es: Si te mareas, sal enseguida y avisa a Nuria.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are reading the spa rules with the attendant, and the AI is your friend Felipe: explain what to do before, during and after each pool and sauna with antes de, después de and hay que, and tell him to read the health warning and ask the staff.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de entrar hay que ducharse)

examples.es: Antes de entrar en el baño de vapor, hay que quitarse el albornoz.
examples.en: Before going into the steam room, you have to take off your bathrobe.

examples.es: Después de usar la piscina fría, hay que secarse bien.
examples.en: After using the cold pool, you have to dry off well.

lessons.title: Mold Behind the Wardrobe: Propose a Fix to the Host
lessons.objective: Describe what you found and what the room was like at arrival, then propose a fair solution to the host.

words.note: Chilean word for earring; arete is used in Mexico.
Standard in Chile and most of Latin America for a hotel or rental stay.
Chileans say departamento; piso is Spain.

words.en: When we arrived, the apartment smelled damp.
words.es: Cuando llegamos, el departamento olía a humedad.
words.note: Preterite for the arrival, imperfect for how it smelled.

words.en: I moved the wardrobe because I dropped an earring.
words.es: Moví el ropero porque se me cayó un aro.

words.en: Behind the wardrobe there was mold all over the wall.
words.es: Detrás del ropero había moho en toda la pared.

words.en: I'll show you the wall on the video call; can you see it well?
words.es: Le muestro la pared por la videollamada; ¿la ve bien?
words.note: Formal usted with the host.

words.en: Maybe last week it wasn't visible, but now it looks like this.
words.es: Quizás la semana pasada no se veía, pero ahora está así.

words.en: Could you send someone to us today to do a deep cleaning?
words.es: ¿Podría mandarnos a alguien hoy para hacer una limpieza profunda?
words.note: Formal. Keep the personal a before alguien.

words.en: If not, a partial refund would be fair.
words.es: Si no, una devolución parcial sería lo justo.

words.en: Hey, take photos of the mold before touching anything.
words.es: Oye, sácale fotos al moho antes de tocar nada.
words.note: Informal tú, to your travel companion.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest, and the AI is Rodrigo, the host, on a video call: describe how the apartment was when you arrived and what you found behind the wardrobe using preterite and imperfect (olía a humedad, encontré), then propose a fair fix with podría and sería.

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (olía a humedad; podría mandarnos a alguien)

examples.es: Cuando entré, la pieza olía a humedad.
examples.en: When I came in, the room smelled damp.

examples.es: ¿Podría mandarnos a alguien esta tarde?
examples.en: Could you send someone to us this afternoon?

lessons.title: Pool Closed for Works: Weigh the Partner Hotel Offer
lessons.objective: Compare the substitute options the hotel offers and say which one the group will take and why.

words.note: Mexican word for pool; piscina is also understood.
Common in Mexico for a shallow children's pool.
Mexican word for pool or beach loungers.
Same word for the lifeguard and the life ring; el or la for the person.

words.en: Until when is the pool going to be closed?
words.es: ¿Hasta cuándo va a estar cerrada la alberca?

words.en: Is the shuttle to the partner hotel going to be free?
words.es: ¿El traslado al hotel asociado va a ser gratis?

words.en: How many wristbands are you going to give us for the group?
words.es: ¿Cuántas pulseras nos van a dar para el grupo?

words.en: For the kids, the kiddie pool will be better than the beach.
words.es: Para los niños, el chapoteadero será mejor que la playa.

words.en: The discount is less practical than the pass, because we want to swim.
words.es: El descuento es menos práctico que el pase, porque queremos nadar.

words.en: The grandparents will be more comfortable there than at the beach.
words.es: Los abuelos estarán más cómodos allá que en la playa.

words.en: Hey, everyone, I think the day pass is going to suit us better.
words.es: Oigan, creo que el pase de día nos va a convenir más.
words.note: Informal, to your family; ustedes is the normal plural in Mexico.

words.en: We'll take the day pass; can you confirm it in writing?
words.es: Tomaremos el pase de día; ¿me lo confirma por escrito?
words.note: Formal usted with the agent.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest speaking for a family group, and the AI is Itzel from guest relations: ask what each offer includes, compare the day pass and the discount with más … que and menos … que, and say which one the group will take using ir a and the future.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (el pase de día va a ser más cómodo que el descuento)

examples.es: Mañana tomaremos el traslado de las 10.
examples.en: Tomorrow we'll take the 10 o'clock shuttle.

examples.es: Los niños se van a divertir más en el hotel asociado que aquí.
examples.en: The kids are going to have more fun at the partner hotel than here.

lessons.title: Police Report After a Backpack Vanishes from Storage
lessons.objective: Tell the police officer what happened step by step and give times, values and serial numbers clearly.

words.note: Peruvian police rank; address him as suboficial.
Common in Peru; la computadora portátil is more formal.
Usual hotel wording in Peru.
Peru's currency, written S/ before the amount.

words.en: the copy of the police report
I left the backpack in storage at 9:10 in the morning.
words.es: Dejé la mochila en custodia a las 9:10 de la mañana.

words.en: When I came back, the backpack was gone.
words.es: Cuando volví, la mochila ya no estaba.

words.en: The serial number is 4471 8820; I'll repeat it for you.
words.es: El número de serie es 4471 8820; se lo repito.
words.note: Read long numbers in pairs or blocks: cuarenta y cuatro, setenta y uno.

words.en: The laptop is worth about 4000 soles, more or less.
words.es: La laptop vale unos 4000 soles, más o menos.

words.en: I don't know the exact time; it was between 11 and 12.
words.es: No sé la hora exacta; fue entre las 11 y las 12.
words.note: If you are not sure, say so instead of guessing.

words.en: Excuse me, can you repeat that more slowly?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿me lo puede repetir más despacio?
words.note: Formal usted with the officer.

words.en: Carmen, can the hotel check the camera recording?
words.es: Carmen, ¿el hotel puede revisar la grabación de las cámaras?

words.en: Can you give me a copy of the report for the insurance?
words.es: ¿Me puede dar una copia de la denuncia para el seguro?

lessons.speaking: You are the guest whose backpack disappeared, and the AI is Suboficial Quispe taking your statement: tell what happened step by step in the preterite (dejé, volví, pedí) and give times, values and serial numbers clearly, repeating each number when asked.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (dejé la mochila a las nueve y diez; el número de serie es…)

examples.es: Entregué la mochila en recepción y me dieron un ticket.
examples.en: I handed in the backpack at reception and they gave me a ticket.

examples.es: Regresé a las 2:30 y pedí la mochila.
examples.en: I came back at 2:30 and asked for the backpack.

lessons.title: Turning Down the Host's Off-Platform Cash Deal
lessons.objective: Politely refuse an improper request, explain why, and suggest a proper alternative through the booking platform.

words.note: Colombians say pagar por fuera de la plataforma.
In Colombia, soporte often means a receipt or proof.
Talk about the risk in general; never call the host a scammer.

words.en: Please don't ask me for passport photos over WhatsApp.
words.es: Por favor, no me pida fotos del pasaporte por WhatsApp.
words.note: Formal usted; normal with a host in Colombia.

words.en: I don't recommend that we pay cash outside the platform.
words.es: No recomiendo que paguemos en efectivo por fuera de la plataforma.
words.note: No recomiendo que takes the subjunctive: paguemos.

words.en: Better to send a change request through the platform.
words.es: Mejor envíe una solicitud de modificación por la plataforma.

words.en: How about we put the extra charge through the platform?
words.es: ¿Le parece si pasamos el cobro adicional por la plataforma?

words.en: It's nothing personal; we prefer that everything is on record.
words.es: No es nada personal; preferimos que todo quede registrado.

words.en: I don't recommend that anyone send documents by chat.
words.es: No recomiendo que nadie mande documentos por chat.

words.en: Don't send him anything yet; let's talk it over first.
words.es: No le manden nada todavía; primero lo hablamos.
words.note: Plural ustedes command, to your group.

words.en: We'll gladly leave you a good review at the end.
words.es: Con mucho gusto le dejamos una buena reseña al final.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest who made the booking, and the AI is Wilson, the host: politely refuse the cash payment and the passport photos with negative commands (no me pida) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, explain why, and suggest doing it through the platform.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no me mande fotos del pasaporte; no recomiendo que paguemos en efectivo)

examples.es: No me pida el efectivo, por favor; páselo por la plataforma.
examples.en: Please don't ask me for the cash; put it through the platform.

examples.es: No recomiendo que mandemos los pasaportes por WhatsApp.
examples.en: I don't recommend that we send the passports over WhatsApp.

lessons.title: Honest Feedback for a New Guesthouse Owner
lessons.objective: Give balanced feedback on the stay and recommend specific changes in a respectful way.

words.note: Feminine for a woman owner; el dueño for a man.
Mexican coffee brewed in a clay pot with cinnamon and piloncillo.
Feminine noun that takes el because it starts with a stressed a.

words.en: The pot-brewed coffee is delicious, really.
words.es: El café de olla está riquísimo, de verdad.

words.en: I hope you keep treating guests so warmly.
words.es: Ojalá que siga con ese trato tan cálido.
words.note: Formal: siga is the usted form.

words.en: I recommend that you open the dining room a little earlier.
words.es: Le recomiendo que abra el comedor un poco más temprano.
words.note: Formal. Le recomiendo que + present subjunctive.

words.en: I suggest you put up a sign with the breakfast hours.
words.es: Le sugiero que ponga un letrero con el horario del desayuno.

words.en: It's important that there's purified water in every room.
words.es: Es importante que haya agua purificada en cada cuarto.

words.en: I understand your reasons, Inés; it's just a suggestion.
words.es: Entiendo sus razones, Inés; es solo una sugerencia.

words.en: It's not a criticism; I want things to go really well for you.
words.es: No es una crítica; quiero que le vaya muy bien.

words.en: I hope the official opening is a big success.
words.es: Ojalá que la apertura oficial sea todo un éxito.

lessons.speaking: You are a guest giving feedback over breakfast, and the AI is Inés Ruiz, the guesthouse owner: praise what works, then recommend specific changes, including the breakfast hours, using le recomiendo que + subjunctive and ojalá que, in a respectful usted tone.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (le recomiendo que ponga; ojalá que siga)

examples.es: Le recomiendo que sirva el desayuno desde las 7:30.
examples.en: I recommend that you serve breakfast from 7:30.

examples.es: Ojalá que siga haciendo ese café de olla.
examples.en: I hope you keep making that pot-brewed coffee.

lessons.title: Mediate Between Your Friend and the Housekeeper
lessons.objective: Report what each side said, explain the background, and help both agree on what happens next.

words.note: Common hotel word in Uruguay and Argentina for a woman housekeeper.
Feminine for a woman; el supervisor for a man.
Rioplatense; Mexico says el buró.
Everyday Rioplatense word for medicine.

words.en: Sofía said the toiletry bag was on the bathroom shelf.
words.es: Sofía dijo que el neceser estaba en la repisa del baño.

words.en: Rosa says she only moved it to the nightstand.
words.es: Rosa dice que solo lo movió a la mesita de luz.

words.en: Rosa explained the shelf was wet, so she moved it.
words.es: Rosa explicó que la repisa estaba mojada y por eso lo movió.

words.en: When we came back, the cleaning cart was still in the hallway.
words.es: Cuando volvimos, el carro de limpieza todavía estaba en el pasillo.

words.en: I think it was a communication problem, not bad faith.
words.es: Creo que fue un problema de comunicación, no de mala fe.

words.en: Graciela, could you check the lost and found, please?
words.es: Graciela, ¿podría revisar en objetos perdidos, por favor?
words.note: Formal (usted) for the supervisor.

words.en: Sofía, tell Graciela where you left it.
words.es: Sofía, contale a Graciela dónde lo dejaste.
words.note: Informal vos command, natural in Uruguay and Argentina.

words.en: How about we look for it in the room now?
words.es: ¿Les parece si lo buscamos en la habitación ahora?

lessons.speaking: You are the guest who heard both sides, and the AI is Graciela, the hotel supervisor: explain Sofía's and Rosa's versions with reported speech (dijo que…, contó que…) and the imperfect for background, then help everyone agree on the next steps.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Sofía dijo que la bolsa estaba en la mesa)

examples.es: Rosa me contó que el neceser estaba abierto en el piso.
examples.en: Rosa told me the toiletry bag was open on the floor.

examples.es: Sofía dijo que tenía sus remedios adentro.
examples.en: Sofía said she had her medicine inside.

lessons.title: Keep the Group Going Through a Road Blockade
lessons.objective: Encourage a tired group, make clear commitments about the plan, and agree on extra nights with the host.

words.note: A general or transport strike; often comes with blockades.
Common in Bolivia for a bus or plane ticket.
Andean word; also el mal de altura.
Common, legal hostel drink in Bolivia.

words.en: Cheer up, guys, we'll sort it out together.
words.note: Informal, to the group.

words.en: Tomorrow at 8 I'll call the travel agency.
words.es: Mañana a las 8 llamaré a la agencia de viajes.

words.en: Tonight I'll find out if the blockades are still on.
words.es: Esta noche averiguaré si siguen los bloqueos.

words.en: Tomás, you rest; I'll take care of everything.
words.es: Tomás, tú descansa; yo me encargaré de todo.
words.note: Informal tú.

words.en: Wara, could we stay 2 more nights?
words.note: Polite conditional, good for the host.

words.en: We'll take the dorm; we'll be fine in the bunk beds.
words.es: Nos quedamos con el dormitorio; estaremos bien en las literas.

words.en: Would you give us a group rate for the 2 nights?
words.es: ¿Nos haría una tarifa grupal por las 2 noches?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'll pay you the advance today, I promise.
words.es: Le pagaré el adelanto hoy mismo, se lo prometo.
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the group's organizer, and the AI plays your tired friends and then Wara, the hostel host: lift the group's spirits with ánimo and the future (llamaré, lo resolveremos), commit to a clear plan, and agree on 2 extra nights with Wara using usted.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (mañana llamaré a la agencia; ánimo, lo resolveremos)

examples.es: Si la carretera sigue cerrada, buscaremos otro pasaje.
examples.en: If the highway stays closed, we'll look for another ticket.

examples.es: Ánimo, Lucía; pronto estaremos en Uyuni.
examples.en: Cheer up, Lucía; we'll be in Uyuni soon.

lessons.title: Register: Manager, Bellhop, Roommate, Booking Agent
lessons.objective: Make the same request four ways, switching between usted and tú and softening it for each listener.

words.note: Same form for singular and plural: el botones, los botones.
Feminine for a woman; el agente for a man.
Feminine for a woman; el compañero for a man.
Softer than quiero; good with managers and agents.
Informal opener with tú; with usted say oiga.

words.en: Mr. Restrepo, I'd like to ask you for a rollaway bed, please.
words.es: Señor Restrepo, quisiera pedirle una cama plegable, por favor.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would it be possible to have it in the room tonight?
words.es: ¿Sería posible tenerla en el cuarto esta noche?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Hey, Kevin, can you give me a hand with the bed?
words.es: Oye, Kevin, ¿me echas una mano con la cama?
words.note: Informal tú.

words.en: Kevin, can you bring it up to 504 when you get a chance?
words.es: Kevin, ¿me la subes a la 504 cuando puedas?
words.note: Informal tú; la 504 means la habitación 504.

words.en: Hey, Dani, do you know if they have rollaway beds here?
words.es: Oye, Dani, ¿sabes si aquí tienen camas plegables?
words.note: Informal, by chat.

words.en: Good afternoon, Paola; I'd like to add a rollaway bed to my booking.
words.es: Buenas tardes, Paola; quisiera agregar una cama plegable a mi reserva.
words.note: Formal, by phone.

words.en: Could you tell me if there's a per-person charge?
words.es: ¿Me podría decir si hay un cargo por persona?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Could you confirm it by email, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo podría confirmar por correo, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You need a rollaway bed, and the AI plays manager Sr. Restrepo, bellhop Kevin, hostel-mate Daniela and booking agent Paola in turn: make the same request to each, switching between usted and tú and softening it with quisiera, ¿sería posible…?, oye and ¿me echas una mano?

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿sería posible…?, oye, ¿me echas una mano?)

examples.es: Quisiera saber si tienen una cama plegable disponible.
examples.en: I'd like to know if you have a rollaway bed available.

examples.es: Oye, ¿me ayudas a subirla al cuarto?
examples.en: Hey, can you help me take it up to the room?

lessons.title: A Friend Slips on the Wet Lobby Stairs
lessons.objective: Tell the duty manager exactly what happened and when, and make sure the incident book records it correctly.

words.note: In Spain, hotels log accidents and problems here. Ask to read the entry before anyone signs it.
Use el responsable de turno for a man.
Spain. Fregar means to mop.
In Spain the floor is el suelo.
Use la testigo for a woman.
Use el limpiador for a man.

words.en: At around 8 we were going down the lobby stairs.
words.es: A eso de las 8 bajábamos por la escalera del vestíbulo.
words.note: Use the imperfect (bajábamos) for the background and the preterite for what happened next.

words.en: Just before that, a cleaner had mopped the steps.
words.es: Justo antes, una limpiadora había fregado los escalones.

words.en: At that moment there was no wet floor sign.
words.es: En ese momento no había ningún cartel de suelo mojado.

words.en: Marcos slipped on the third step and fell sideways.
words.es: Marcos se resbaló en el tercer escalón y cayó de lado.

words.en: Right after that, his right ankle started to hurt a lot.
words.es: Justo después, empezó a dolerle mucho el tobillo derecho.

words.en: Easy, Marcos, don't move; help is on the way.
words.es: Tranquilo, Marcos, no te muevas; ya vienen a ayudarte.
words.note: Informal, to your friend.

words.en: Elena, could you read me what you've written in the book, please?
words.es: Elena, ¿me lee lo que ha escrito en el libro, por favor?
words.note: Formal, to the manager.

words.en: Please also note the exact time of the fall.
words.es: Por favor, anote también la hora exacta de la caída.
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are Marcos's friend, and the AI is Elena Vidal, the duty manager writing the report: tell her step by step what happened using a eso de las 8, justo después and en ese momento, and check that the incident book records it correctly.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a eso de las ocho, justo después, en ese momento)

examples.es: A eso de las 8 y 10, Marcos bajó por la escalera.
examples.en: At around 8:10, Marcos went down the stairs.

examples.es: Justo después de la caída, llamé a recepción.
examples.en: Right after the fall, I called the front desk.

lessons.title: Loose Balcony Railing: Talk Through a Near Miss
lessons.objective: Explain what almost happened and what could have happened, without blame, and agree on a fix with maintenance.

words.note: Where the railing is fixed to the wall or floor.
Common phrase: nos llevamos un buen susto (we got a real scare).

words.en: He very nearly leaned on the balcony railing.
words.es: Por poco se apoya en la barandilla del balcón.
words.note: Por poco + present tense describes something in the past that almost happened.

words.en: Lucas almost leaned on it, but I saw him just in time.
words.es: Lucas casi se apoya, pero lo vi justo a tiempo.

words.en: If I hadn't seen him, he could have fallen from here.
words.es: Si no lo veo, podría haberse caído desde aquí.
words.note: In speech, si + present often replaces si + pluperfect for past events.

words.en: Yeray, it's not your fault; I'm just telling you what happened.
words.es: Yeray, no es culpa suya; solo le cuento lo que pasó.
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: If someone leans on it now, it could come loose completely.
words.es: Si alguien se apoya ahora, podría soltarse del todo.

words.en: In the meantime, can we put up tape and close the sliding door?
words.es: Mientras tanto, ¿podemos poner cinta y cerrar la puerta corredera?

words.en: Kids, don't go out on the balcony until they fix it.
words.es: Chicos, no salgan al balcón hasta que lo arreglen.
words.note: Informal, to the group. In the Canary Islands, ustedes is used even with friends.

words.en: When could you do the permanent repair?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the adult in charge of the group, and the AI is Yeray, the maintenance worker: explain what almost happened using casi, por poco and podría haber, keep it free of blame, and agree on a temporary and a permanent fix.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco se apoya; si no lo veo, podría haberse caído)

examples.es: Por poco se apoya en la barandilla suelta.
examples.en: He nearly leaned on the loose railing.

examples.es: Si no lo veo a tiempo, podría haber sido grave.
examples.en: If I hadn't seen him in time, it could have been serious.

lessons.title: Water Through the Ceiling: The Night Emergency Call
lessons.objective: Call the 24-hour line, describe the leak near the outlets, follow short instructions, and agree what happens next.

words.note: Mexico. Spain says la regleta.
Mexico. Enchufe is also understood.
Mexico. Many people also say el breaker.
Mexico. Don Chuy is a respectful nickname, so use usted with him.
Mexico.
Mexico.
Mexico. Ask for it so you can follow up on the case.

words.en: I'm calling from 302; water is coming down from the ceiling.
words.es: Le llamo del 302; está cayendo agua del techo.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: The drip is right next to the power strip.
words.es: La gotera está justo al lado del multicontacto.

words.en: If the water reaches the outlet, I don't touch it, right?
words.es: Si el agua llega al contacto, no lo toco, ¿verdad?

words.en: I won't touch anything electrical until you tell me to.
words.es: No toco nada eléctrico hasta que usted me diga.

words.en: We already put a bucket and rags on the floor.
words.es: Ya pusimos una cubeta y trapos en el piso.
words.note: In Mexico the floor is el piso.

words.en: If they cut the power, we'll go down to the night guard.
words.es: Si cortan la luz, bajaremos con el velador.
words.note: In Mexico, la luz also means the electricity.

words.en: If it doesn't stop in 10 minutes, I'll call you again.
words.es: Si no para en 10 minutos, la volveré a llamar.
words.note: La, because Brenda is a woman. Use lo for a man.

words.en: Can you give me the report number, please?
words.es: ¿Me da el número de folio, por favor?

lessons.speaking: You are the guest in apartment 302, and the AI is Brenda from the 24-hour line: describe the leak next to the power strip, repeat back her short instructions, and agree on next steps using si + present → future (si cortan la luz, bajaremos).

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short phone commands (si el agua llega al enchufe, no lo toque; si cortan la luz, bajaremos)

examples.es: Si el agua llega al multicontacto, no lo toque.
examples.en: If the water reaches the power strip, don't touch it.

examples.es: Si Don Chuy encuentra la llave de paso, la cerrará enseguida.
examples.en: If Don Chuy finds the shutoff valve, he'll close it right away.

lessons.title: A City Inspector Checks Your Rental's License
lessons.objective: Answer a city inspector's formal questions about the booking, key handover and guest registration.

words.note: It's normal and polite to ask to see it before you answer.
Spain. Mexico says el departamento.
Spain.
In Spain, hosts must register guests with the authorities.
Feminine noun that takes el: el acta, las actas.
Spain.

words.en: Good morning; could you show me your ID badge, please?
words.es: Buenos días; ¿me enseña su acreditación, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: The flat was booked through the platform in March.
words.es: El piso se reservó por la plataforma en marzo.

words.en: The keys were handed to us on Monday afternoon.
words.es: Se nos entregaron las llaves el lunes por la tarde.

words.en: The host, Núria, isn't answering her phone right now.
words.es: La anfitriona, Núria, no contesta al teléfono ahora mismo.

words.en: There are 3 of us staying here, all adults.
I'll give you my name and my passport number.
words.es: Le doy mi nombre y mi número de pasaporte.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'd rather not give my personal phone number; is it required?
words.es: Prefiero no dar mi teléfono personal; ¿es obligatorio?
words.note: A polite way to decline. Ask whether it's required instead of refusing outright.

words.en: Could you give me a copy of the report, please?
words.es: ¿Me podría dar una copia del acta, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest, and the AI is Jordi Puig, a city inspector: answer his formal questions about the booking, key handover and guest registration with usted and the passive se (se reservó, se nos entregaron), and politely decline to give data you aren't required to share.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se reservó por la plataforma; se nos entregaron las llaves)

examples.es: Se nos pidieron los pasaportes para el registro de viajeros.
examples.en: We were asked for our passports for the guest registration.

examples.es: El pago se hizo por la plataforma, no en efectivo.
examples.en: The payment was made through the platform, not in cash.

lessons.title: Write an Official Complaint Form at a Madrid Hotel
lessons.objective: Write a clear, formal complaint with facts, dates, the hotel's response and your request, and keep a stamped copy.

words.note: Ask for it by this exact name in Spain; hotels keep it at the front desk.
More formal than queja; it is the word used on official forms.
Many people in Spain also say el overbooking.
Spain: the code on your booking confirmation.
Formal written word for the hotel or business.

words.en: Good evening, Álvaro; could you give me the complaint form, please?
words.es: Buenas noches, Álvaro; ¿me facilita la hoja de reclamaciones, por favor?
words.note: Formal; facilitar is the usual polite verb in Spain.

words.en: First, nobody showed up to pick us up at the airport.
words.es: En primer lugar, nadie se presentó a recogernos en el aeropuerto.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: Next, we were told that the room was occupied.
words.es: A continuación, se nos informó de que la habitación estaba ocupada.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: It should be noted that the booking was confirmed and paid.
words.es: Cabe señalar que la reserva estaba confirmada y pagada.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: Therefore, I request a refund of the taxi costs.
words.es: Por lo tanto, solicito el reembolso de los gastos de taxi.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: Please write the hotel's response here.
words.es: Le ruego que escriba aquí la respuesta del establecimiento.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Álvaro, can you confirm the exact time I arrived?
words.es: Álvaro, ¿me confirma la hora exacta en que llegué?

words.en: Could you stamp the customer's copy, please?
words.es: ¿Me sella el ejemplar para el cliente, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest, and the AI is Álvaro, the receptionist: ask for the hoja de reclamaciones, dictate the facts in order with en primer lugar, a continuación, cabe señalar que and por lo tanto, state your request, and ask for a stamped copy.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, a continuación, por lo tanto, cabe señalar que)

examples.es: Cabe señalar que el hotel no ofreció ninguna alternativa.
examples.en: It should be noted that the hotel offered no alternative.

examples.es: Por lo tanto, solicito una indemnización por los gastos ocasionados.
examples.en: Therefore, I request compensation for the costs incurred.

lessons.title: WhatsApp and Voice Notes: Splitting the Group Arrival
lessons.objective: Coordinate a split arrival and parking by text and voice note, using local messaging style and polite requests.

words.note: Argentina: mandame un audio = send me a voice note.
Argentina: a covered parking spot or garage.
Argentina: a car with a driver booked by phone, often at a fixed price.
Argentina: a highway, as in la ruta 68.
Rural Argentina: the gate at the entrance of a farm or estate.
Argentina: the money paid to hold a booking.
Dejar en visto = to read a message without replying.
Argentina says ómnibus or micro for a long-distance bus.
Informal Argentine yes; very common in messages.

words.en: Hi, Mercedes! Would it work for you if we arrive in 2 groups?
words.es: ¡Hola, Mercedes! ¿Te vendría bien que lleguemos en 2 tandas?
words.note: Polite conditional; the form is the same with vos and tú.

words.en: Half the group arrives tonight by hired car.
words.es: La mitad del grupo llega esta noche en remís.

words.en: The other 3 arrive tomorrow with the rental car.
words.es: Los otros 3 llegan mañana con el auto alquilado.

words.en: Could you keep the parking space free for us tomorrow afternoon?
words.es: ¿Podrías dejarnos la cochera libre para mañana a la tarde?
words.note: Argentina says a la tarde for in the afternoon.

words.en: Sorry, could you send it to me in writing? I don't have a good signal.
words.es: Perdón, ¿me lo podrías mandar por escrito, que no tengo buena señal?

words.en: Can you send me the location of the gate?
words.es: ¿Me mandás la ubicación de la tranquera?
words.note: Informal vos form, normal with an Argentine host on WhatsApp.

words.en: Would you mind waiting for us at the gate around 11?
words.es: ¿Te molestaría esperarnos en la tranquera a eso de las 11?

words.en: OK, I'll send you a voice note when we leave the terminal.
words.es: Dale, te mando un audio cuando salgamos de la terminal.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are the group organizer, and the AI is Mercedes, the guesthouse host, replying by voice note: explain the split arrival, ask for parking and directions with ¿te vendría bien…? and ¿podrías dejarnos…?, and confirm the times in short messages.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿te vendría bien…?, ¿podrías dejarnos…?)

examples.es: ¿Te vendría bien recibirnos a las 10 de la noche?
examples.en: Would it work for you to receive us at 10 p.m.?

examples.es: ¿Podrías dejarnos un lugar en la cochera para el auto?
examples.en: Could you leave us a spot in the garage for the car?

lessons.title: Checkout Walkthrough with the Host and a Broken Lamp
lessons.objective: Walk the flat with the host, point out a broken lamp and old marks, and agree on terms before you hand back the keys.

words.note: Spain; Latin America says el foco.
Spain: the deposit on a rental, returned after checkout.
Spain; you will also see it written el tique.
Spain's instant bank-to-bank payment app; pagar por Bizum.

words.en: Iñaki, before we leave, I wanted to tell you about the lamp.
words.es: Iñaki, antes de irnos, quería comentarle lo de la lámpara.
words.note: Formal (usted) with the host.

words.en: The floor lamp fell over and the shade broke.
words.es: Se nos cayó la lámpara de pie y se rompió la pantalla.
words.note: Se nos cayó presents it as an accident, which sounds honest and natural.

words.en: We would pay for it ourselves, as long as you send us the receipt.
words.es: La pagaríamos nosotros, siempre que nos mande el ticket.

words.en: This stain was already here when we arrived; here are the photos.
words.es: Esta mancha ya estaba cuando llegamos; aquí tiene las fotos.

words.en: Would you take it out of the deposit instead of charging it separately?
words.es: ¿Lo descontaría usted de la fianza, en vez de cobrarlo aparte?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: These floor scratches would be normal wear and tear, don't you think?
words.es: Estos arañazos del suelo serían desgaste normal, ¿no cree?

words.en: Ana, pull up the arrival photos on your phone, please.
words.es: Ana, saca las fotos de la llegada del móvil, porfa.
words.note: Informal, to a friend; porfa is casual.

words.en: We'll give you back the keys as soon as everything is in writing.
words.es: Le devolvemos las llaves en cuanto quede todo por escrito.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest, and the AI is Iñaki, the host: walk the flat together, admit the broken lamp, show your arrival photos of the stain, and agree on payment using the conditional with siempre que or en caso de que before you hand back the keys.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (lo pagaríamos siempre que nos envíe el recibo)

examples.es: Pagaríamos la pantalla siempre que nos envíe una foto del ticket.
examples.en: We would pay for the shade as long as you send us a photo of the receipt.

examples.es: En caso de que le preocupe la mancha, le enviaríamos las fotos de la llegada.
examples.en: In case the stain worries you, we would send you the arrival photos.

lessons.title: Capstone: Moving a Group Between Lodgings in One Day
lessons.objective: Run a hard moving day: brief the group, solve problems, handle an incident, report it, and close both stays in Spanish.

words.note: Ecuador: a van or pickup truck.
Ecuador uses the US dollar.
Latin America says vidrio; Spain says cristal.
¿Necesita puntos? = Does it need stitches?

words.en: Guys, bring everything down to the lobby before 11, please.
words.es: Chicos, bajen todo al lobby antes de las 11, porfa.
words.note: Plural ustedes command to the group; informal.

words.en: Patricio, can you confirm there's no outstanding balance?
words.es: Patricio, ¿me confirma que no queda ningún saldo pendiente?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Gabriela, the key box won't open; do you have a backup code?
words.es: Gabriela, la caja de llaves no abre; ¿tiene un código de respaldo?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: While the locksmith is on the way, could we leave the suitcases somewhere?
words.es: Mientras llega el cerrajero, ¿podríamos dejar las maletas en algún lado?

words.en: Andrés, press the gauze hard and don't let go.
words.es: Andrés, aprieta la gasa fuerte y no la sueltes.
words.note: Informal tú command to a friend.

words.en: If it doesn't stop bleeding, we're going to the emergency room.
words.es: Si no deja de sangrar, vamos a la sala de emergencias.

words.en: At around 4, Andrés cut himself on a glass.
words.es: A eso de las 4, Andrés se cortó con un vaso.

words.en: I'll write to you in the group chat as soon as we have keys.
words.es: Les escribo en el chat del grupo en cuanto tengamos llaves.

lessons.speaking: You are the group leader, and the AI is night manager Patricio, host Gabriela and your friend Andrés in turn: close the checkout, get into the rental, help Andrés with clear tú commands, report what happened in past tenses, and message everyone using cuando + subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar

examples.es: Patricio dijo que nos guardaría las maletas hasta que llegara la camioneta.
examples.en: Patricio said he would keep our bags until the van arrived.

examples.es: Cuando lleguemos al departamento, revisen que todos tengan sus cosas.
examples.en: When we get to the apartment, check that everyone has their things.
